Details
This guidance provides information and outlines the core engineering and mathematics knowledge required for restricted, management level Certificates of Competency (STCW III/2 and III/3). The MCA General Engineering Science examinations are currently delegated to the International Association of Maritime Institutions (IAMI).
This is guidance to all Owners, Masters, Officers, Ratings and those concerned with maritime training. This guidance should be read with with MSN 1857 - Amendment 1 , MSN 1904 and replaces the syllabus published on UK seafarer careers: Training provision, information and examination syllabuses .

Transposition of formulae
mc-TY-transposition-2009-1
In mathematics, engineering and science, formulae are used to relate physical quantities to each other. They provide rules so that if we know the values of certain quantities, we can calculate the values of others. In this unit we discuss how formulae can be transposed, or transformed, or rearranged.
In order to master the techniques explained here it is vital that you undertake plenty of practice exercises so that they become second nature.
After reading this text, and/or viewing the video tutorial on this topic, you should be able to:
• transpose formulae in order to make other variables the subject of the formula
3. Transposition of simple formulae
Example
Consider the formula v = u + at. Suppose we wish to transpose this formula to obtain one for t.
Because we want to obtain t on its own we start by subtracting u from each side:
v = u + at v − u = at
We now divide everything on both sides by a. v − u

The Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) owns the certification framework; the General Engineering Science written examinations are administered by the International Association of Maritime Institutions (IAMI). What topics are on the GES I syllabus? Mathematics (fractions/ratios, algebra, graphs, trigonometry, geometry/mensuration) and Applied Mechanics (kinematics, dynamics, statics, friction, machines, strength of materials), as published on GOV.UK. Is the official exam multiple choice? No. GES I sections are Applied Mechanics and Mathematics (MIN 565). Pass requires ≥40% in each section and ≥50% overall.
